subject: Large data.frame with large number of grouping levels

messages.author: 4b880dbd85e89f08
messages.subject: Large data.frame with large number of grouping levels
parts:
Hi all,

As far as I can tell (and I am new to plyr so please do bear with me
if I am wrong), I think there is a "bug" in the sense that:

### START CODE

library(plyr)
rm(list=ls())

df <- data.frame (x1 = rep(1:1000,2), x2=rep(1:1000,2), x3=rep(1:500,4))
df$dat<-rnorm(nrow(df))
# works as expected
sumdat1 <- ddply(df, c("x1", "x2", "x3"), summarize, meandat = mean(dat))

nrow(sumdat1) # 1000
sumdat1[1,4] == (df$dat[1]+df$dat[1001])/2 # TRUE

# too big, does not work
df <- data.frame (x1 = rep(1:10000,2), x2=rep(1:10000,2), x3=rep(1:5000,4))
df$dat<-rnorm(nrow(df))
# warning message and wrong output
sumdat2 <- ddply(df, c("x1", "x2", "x3"), summarize, meandat = mean(dat))

# Warning message:
# In id(splits, drop = drop) : NAs introduced by coercion

nrow(sumdat2)  # I get 44 rows instead of 10000
sumdat2[1,4] == (df$dat[1]+df$dat[10001])/2 # TRUE (as expected)

### END CODE

Similarly if I do

### START CODE

for (ind in 1:1000) {
a<-data.frame(x1=rnorm(200*ind), x2=rnorm(200*ind))
if (sum(is.na(id(a)))>0) break()
}

### breaks at iteration 232

### END CODE

Looks to me like when I use the ddply call, it calls id (or
equivalent) on the variables that are used to split the data.frame,
and because those variables are too long, the numeric vector ends up
with NAs, and bad things happen.

In case this is expected behavior, may I suggest some kind of warning
to the user that some row limit (and/or number of different "splits")
has been crossed. I know I spent a while trying to work out what was going on.

Thanks!

Best,
Anirban
